source: US Dam Hazard Classification - Corrected Edition (2026-11-09), Appendix A

R1.name: Transient-use exclusion
R1.rule: People only occasionally or briefly present do not by themselves create probable life loss.
R1.source: FEMA 333; New York; Rhode Island (incidental presence); Arizona three-part test

R2.name: Occupancy presumption
R2.rule: Habitable structures (incl. regularly occupied farm/commercial, overnight recreation) are assumed occupied; occasionally used outbuildings are not. A home shown flooded is assumed flooded above its lowest occupied floor unless data show otherwise (New York).
R2.notes: floor_presumption true (New York): a home shown flooded with no floor data is taken as flooded above its lowest occupied floor (its ground depth is used at the floor datum). false: no presumption; a missing floor elevation is a missing input.

R3.name: No evacuation credit
R3.rule: Emergency action plans and evacuation do not lower the class.

R4.name: Dams in series
R4.rule: Where an upstream failure could cause or contribute to a downstream failure, the upstream class is at least the downstream class.
R4.source: Nebraska ('must'); advisory in North Dakota and New York ('should')

R5.name: Future development
R5.source: North Dakota; Virginia; Arizona (10-yr zoning); NRCS

R6.name: Proximity rule for new dams
R6.rule: A new dam within the distance of a city class is designed to High unless downstream development is legally curtailed.

R7.name: Borderline goes higher
R7.rule: A borderline result takes the higher class. Judgment-zone hits from M1 are always flagged.

R8.name: Simplified-analysis limits
R8.rule: Without a breach model a class below High can be justified only for dams storing under the limit at top of dam; lowering from High needs TM-11-based unsteady modeling (New York).
R8.notes: variant storage_limit (North Dakota): no breach model and storage at or over storage_acft_limit (or unknown) -> High. variant lowering_from_high (New York): a dam whose current class is High is not lowered unless the analysis is TM-11-based unsteady modeling (analysis = unsteady_tm11).

R9.name: Incremental damage analysis scope
R9.rule: North Dakota: may reduce the inflow design flood but never the hazard class. Virginia: may lower a proposed class (4VAC50-20-52).

R10.name: Re-review trigger
R10.rule: Store the run date and receptor-layer versions; re-run when downstream layers change.
R10.source: Colorado Rule 5.4; Arizona; Rhode Island; New York; MSHA
